Confirmed — no real calls there, just a comment. That finalizes my list of 34 caller files.

The predicate is `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`. I traced every reference to it and separated genuine call sites from three distractor patterns the codebase deliberately sets up: (1) files that only build a `FlagContext` (`buildFlagContext`, `flagContextFor`, `orgFlagContext`) without calling `isEnabled` themselves, (2) files that only produce or hold a precomputed `FeatureFlagSnapshot` via `snapshotFlags()` (`layout.tsx`, `_lib/tenant-context.ts`) or read one via `readFlag()` (`use-feature-flag.ts`, `feature-gate.tsx`), and (3) `feature-gate.tsx`, which renders a gate without invoking the predicate itself. The defining file `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` was also excluded since its only internal use is the snapshot-building loop and an unused `assertEnabled` wrapper — not a caller.
